sections.lever checks:
- Family and target: who belongs where across two CAMAC publications (the 2012 report and the 2014 discussion paper); one member's proposal is dated only by another submitter's answer; hard (the page shows only Hard open); quick test survived (user chat, 2026-10-14, "only i09 survived"); difficulty result pending.
- Dependency plan: Doc 2 l474-483 (Option 3 of the 2014 paper, backed) -> c1. Doc 2 l631 (the 2014 paper's seven-business-day suggestion, opposed by Allens) + Doc 15 l237-239 (the same test adopted, CAMAC named, no year) -> c2.
- Universe: every "CAMAC" mention in the bundle (listed by search, 2026-10-14) sits in five submissions. D02 AIMA: 2012 report (tailored insolvency regime l410-411; statutory limited liability l434-436; footnotes "CAMAC MIS Report July 2012"; a March 2000 CAMAC paper in footnote 5), backed. D03 AIOFP: "We support the CAMAC recommendation in the 2012 report" (l127). D04 Allens: 2014 discussion paper (Option 3 backed l483; the liquidity suggestion opposed l631; related-party concerns l843, Allens supports a review of those provisions); 2012 report (simple majority, footnote 47, not adopted; "unreasonably inhibit", l612, queried; limited liability, l791 and l799, agreed). D09 ASCF: "the CAMAC suggestion" (l67), opposed. D14 Joint Associations: the liquidity test (l237), adopted. No other submitter names CAMAC. Members: Allens, Joint Associations.
- Necessity: Doc 2 is the only source of Allens' Option 3 support and the only document that dates the liquidity suggestion to 2014 (D09 calls it "the CAMAC suggestion", no year; D14 prints no year). Without Doc 2 the answer is "none" or the Joint Associations by guess. Doc 15 is the only submitter adopting the test; without it the answer is Allens alone. Both are answer components. D02, D03 and D09 hold only candidates that fail and are not ticked (a document that only introduces its own failing candidate is not necessary).
- Selected-lever checks: which-items decoys: ASCF (names CAMAC's suggestion, opposes it); AIMA and AIOFP (back CAMAC, but its 2012 report); AIMA's compliance-plan idea (like Option 3, no CAMAC source). Exclusion recomputed: without "2014" the answer is AIMA, AIOFP, Allens, Joint Associations; without "naming CAMAC" a content reading could add AIMA; with explicit 2014 citations only, Allens alone.
- Targeted failure modes: Linking across documents / Wrong members in a list: "Allens" alone (Doc 15 l237 gives no year; only Doc 2 l631 dates the test). Considered and not declared: Wrong year or edition (adding AIMA or AIOFP for 2012 citations): both print "2012" beside CAMAC, so the wording rules it out for a careful reader; keep to the lazy-default answer until a capture shows otherwise.
- Calculation verification: not applicable (membership).
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: no passage names both members; the bundle overview mentions CAMAC for no document. Searching "2014" reaches Doc 2 only (D14 never prints 2014). Shortest complete route: Doc 2 l483 and l631, then Doc 15 l237.
- Precision/readings: "a proposal from CAMAC's 2014 discussion paper" puts the year on the proposal, not on the submitter's citation. "Naming CAMAC as its source": Doc 15 writes "Corporations and Markets Authority Committee (CAMAC)"; the acronym and the identical test (also called "the CAMAC suggestion" in D09) tie it to CAMAC. "Back": Allens backs Option 3 and opposes the liquidity test; one backed proposal is enough ("a proposal").
- Completeness: no source gaps; all fifteen documents read in full.
- Style/set review: one live question on this bundle. Reserve sketch "accept the liquid-assets definition but rename 'liquid'" uses the same answers 17 and would show the solver the 2014 link: do not submit both.
- Warnings answered: see the hand-over.

sections.question: Which submitters, if any, back a proposal from CAMAC's 2014 discussion paper while naming CAMAC as its source? List them alphabetically.
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 2, Allens' answer on compliance plans): Allens sets out the three reform options in CAMAC's 2014 discussion paper and says "We would support adopting Option 3 proposed in the 2014 CAMAC Discussion Paper", the option that subsumes compliance into risk management with no compliance plan. Allens backs a proposal from that paper and names CAMAC as its source (component c1).

Step 2. Source input (Doc 2, Allens' answer on the definition of liquid assets): Allens says the consultation paper "also refers to the 2014 CAMAC Discussion Paper", in which "CAMAC suggested" a more objective test of liquidity: an asset that can reasonably be expected to be realised for its book value within seven business days. Allens argues against that test.

Step 3. Source input (Doc 15, the Joint Associations' answer on the definition of liquid assets): the Joint Associations recommend that "the objective test of liquidity as suggested by the Corporations and Markets Authority Committee (CAMAC) should be adopted": liquid assets are money, bank accepted bills and assets that can reasonably be expected to be realised for their book value within seven business days. They name CAMAC as the source and give no year.

Step 4. Combination (Doc 2 and Doc 15): the test the Joint Associations back is the one Allens places in CAMAC's 2014 discussion paper (the same objective test, realisation at book value within seven business days). So the Joint Associations also back a proposal from that paper and name CAMAC as its source (component c2).

Step 5. Exclusions, from the other submissions that cite CAMAC: AIMA and AIOFP back recommendations of a different CAMAC publication, its earlier report on managed investment schemes. AIMA's own proposal to reconsider compliance plans resembles Option 3 but names no CAMAC source. Allens' agreement with a recommendation of that earlier report on limited liability does not count; its endorsement from the discussion paper is Option 3.

Decoy: ASCF quotes the same seven-business-day test as "the CAMAC suggestion" but opposes it, so it names CAMAC without backing the proposal.

Final answer, in alphabetical order (Doc 2 and Doc 15): Allens, Joint Associations (CA ANZ, CPA Australia, IPA, SMSF Association).
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Linking across documents
How a careless solver fails: Wrong members in a list

Why these are traps: Linking across documents: Doc 15 adopts CAMAC's seven-business-day liquidity test without saying which CAMAC paper proposed it; only Doc 2's liquid-assets answer places it in the 2014 discussion paper. Counting only explicit 2014 citations gives Allens alone and misses the Joint Associations.
